Commentary.Commentary: So, that is it from the first day of the Super Four stage! Pakistan edged out Afghanistan in a close encounter while India toppled Bangladesh quite comfortably. Next up, on Sunday, we have mouth-watering contests coming your way. Afghanistan will be taking on Bangladesh whereas India will lock horns with Pakistan. Both games will begin at 1530 local (1130 GMT). Till then, goodbye and take care.

Man of the Match, Shoaib Malik, says being a senior player, he knows that when they are chasing such a target and moreover, after a good partnership between Babar Azam and Imam-ul-Haq, his job mainly was to stay at the crease till the end. Also adds that he was confident that if they bat till the end then they will win as they have some hard-hitters lower down the order who can hit the big shots. States that the bowlers are generally confident bowling in the middle overs and are in a lookout to take wickets. But feels that during the final stages of an innings or a match, the bowlers are nervous of going for runs and are not as dangerous as they are in the middle overs. Ends by saying that Afghanistan are a very good side and they have been improving every day.

Pakistan captain, Sarfraz Ahmed, also thanks the almighty first. Adds that they were nervous after losing Fakhar Zaman early but credits the partnership between Babar Azam and Imam-ul-Haq and also feels that Shoaib Malik's innings at the end was special. Admits that Afghanistan batted very sensibly and managed to set up a good target. Mentions that Afghanistan have three of the world's best spinners and any target above 250 on such pitches was always going to be challenging. Lauds his team for pulling off a win. States that they went in with an extra batsman as they wanted to strengthen their batting. Applauds Shoaib Malik for his performance and says his experience is very precious for them. Further adds that he is happy with the win and the team is feeling motivated after today's win. Ends by saying that of late their fielding has improved but today they misfielded a lot and also dropped a few catches and admits that they have to improve going forward.

Afghanistan captain, Asghar Afghan, thanks the Almighty first. Congratulates the Pakistan team for the victory. Adds further that it was a thrilling game and the crowd must have enjoyed a lot. States that this was the first close game of the tournament, so far. Credits Babar Azam and Imam-ul-Haq for the way they played after the early departure of Fakhar Zaman. Admits that had Shoaib Malik's catch been taken by Shahzad then the result could have been different. Ends by saying that Pakistan needed around 40 runs off the last 4 overs and they felt that it would be tough to chase it down but Pakistan played really well to get to the target.

Afghanistan started choking the flow of runs and also managed to pick wickets at regular intervals. Rashid Khan once again was the tormentor-in-chief picking up a three-fer. Mujeeb was also excellent throughout his spell. They bowled exceptionally to bring the equation down to 39 in the last 4 overs. Asif Ali and Mohammad Nawaz didn't play big knocks but hit a maximum each to narrow down the runs required. When these two departed, Afghanistan sniffed in a chance to get their first ODI win over Pakistan but that was not meant to be.  A vital biggie from Hasan in the penultimate over and Shoaib Malik's calm and composed approach in the final ensured Pakistan got over the line with three balls to spare.

During the chase, Afghanistan pegged Pakistan back early by dismissing Fakhar Zaman for a duck. However, Imam-ul-Haq and Babar Azam joined forces and the two showed great resolve in dealing with the Afghan bowlers, especially their spinners. The pair stitched in a massive 154-run stand and put Pakistan on the front foot. Both got to their half centuries and once they did so, they stepped on the accelerator. When the two were batting, Pakistan looked on course for an easy win but a run out changed the course of the whole game. Post that, Rashid got the better of Babar Azam and Afghanistan found themselves back in the game.

First, it was Afghanistan, who batted and managed to put up a competitive total on the board, courtesy Shahidi's unbeaten 97. He anchored the innings quite diligently and the rest played around him. Along with Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah first stitched a 63-run stand and then, his partnership with skipper, Asghar, helped Afghanistan cross the 250-run mark. A total which they were very pleased with at the half-way stage.

WHAT A THRILLER! Humdinger, nail-biter, call it whatever you want to. Feel sorry for the Afghan players, a few of them are down on the ground in tears but you have to credit Shoaib Malik, who showed nerves of steel, took it upon himself by rejecting a single off the very first ball and then finishing it with a maximum and a four. That is what you expect from someone who has so much experience. Brilliant! Don't forget, Shoaib Malik was dropped on 11 by Mohammad Shahzad and it truly cost them the match.

FOUR! All over, PAKISTAN WIN BY 3 WICKETS! Malik has done it. Alam delivers it full and on middle, Shoaib gets across the stumps and whips it behind backward square leg for the winning runs. He also brings up his 42nd ODI fifty with that shot! He is a man for the crisis for Pakistan. Sarfraz in the dressing room screams in joy, Hasan is all pumped up. The batsmen hug each other in the middle. Some sad Afghanistan players in tears. Aftab Alam is down on his haunches, he is absolutely gutted and Malik is seen consoling him. Great gesture. Commiseration, Afghanistan. Congratulations, Pakistan. The crowd is going bonkers. Excellent scenes. Let me slip in a cliched line - Cricket is the real winner.

SIX! That's colossal! Alam drags his length short and lands it on middle, Malik turns inside the crease and rockets it over square leg for a biggie. This is experience for you. What a player! 4 needed off 4 balls.
Well bowled. Too full in length and outside off, Malik drives it straight to covers and sends Hasan back who was eyeing a single.
10 needed off 6 balls. Afghanistan scored 14 in their last over, can Pakistan get 4 less? Malik is on strike and one would expect him to finish it. Can the bowler keep his cool?

Play and a miss! A wrong 'un landing outside off, and spinning back in a touch, Ali attempts for the slog sweep but fails to connect. That wasn't far away from the off pole. 8 runs off Rashid's final over along with a wicket. 10-0-46-3, his figures tonight.
Flatter and on off, skidding through, Ali tries to cut but misses.
SIX! Hasan Ali has dismissed it. Wow, what a clean strike. A flighted full ball around off, Ali goes down on one knee and muscles it over mid-wicket for a biggie.
Hasan Ali joins Malik in the middle.

OUT! Boom! Rashid, you superstar! He sends it flat and quicker through the air. It lands around leg and scoots through off the surface. Nawaz tries to power it across the line but misses to find his stumps disturbed. 16 needed off 9 balls.
Dances down the track to a full ball and heaves it over mid-wicket. Only a single.
Quicker one around middle and leg, Nawaz swings and gets it away through square leg for a run.
Big over! This will probably decide the game. Rashid to bowl. One can feel the tension here.
Finds the yorker around middle and leg, Nawaz tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It rolls on the off side and they cross. 11 from the over, 18 more needed off 12 balls.

SIX! This was on the cards! Alam was getting a bit predictable with his slower ones. As soon as he drops it short, Nawaz attacks it with all his power and sends it packing over wide long on. An 82m hit!
Fine yorker, hitting the blockhole, no room for the batsman to free his arms. Malik digs it out at the last moment. It hits him on the pads before deflecting on the off side and they steal a single.
Too full in length and outside off, Malik drives it to deep cover and takes a brace.
Slight delay as the bowler and captain are having a chat over where to keep the fielders. The overrate is already very poor but no one cares these days.
Gives no pace on this delivery as he serves it on a fuller length outside off. Nawaz drags it off the inner half of the bat to long on for one.
Dot ball. Angles in a length ball from 'round the wicket, Nawaz defends it back to the bowler.
This over will be targeted, one can sense. Aftab Alam has the ball in his hand.

Risky second run! Dipping onto the batsman, a low full toss, Malik gets forward and across before flicking it through mid-wicket. He scampers back for the second run as the fielder releases his throw at the striker's end. The keeper, however, breaks the stumps before collecting the ball. 29 required off 18 balls.
A wrong 'un landing around middle and skidding through, Nawaz at the last moment brings his bat down and keeps it out towards backward point. A sharp single stolen.
Dot ball. Flatter and shorter around off, Nawaz gets across the stumps to work it on the leg side but gets an inside edge onto the front pad.
Mohammad Nawaz is the new batsman.

OUT! Asif Ali holes out! Rashid strikes back. This game is going right down to the wire, folks. A quicker one by the leggie, fuller and outside off, Asif targets the long off stand this time but gets more elevation than distance. Aftab Alam in the deep makes no mistake.
SIX! That's big! Gigantic. Told you, this boy can hit big. A flighted ball around off, turning back in, Ali goes down on one knee and smokes it over mid-wicket for a maximum. 32 needed off 22 balls.
Flatter and shorter on off, Malik goes back and hits it against the spin to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Rashid Khan is back on. He has two overs left. 39 needed off 24 balls. Interesting finish, this.

That wasn't very far away from the stumps! Tossed up ball on off, turning in, Asif gets back and blocks it off the inside edge. The ball drops in front of the sticks and goes closely past the leg pole.

A mishit! Mujeeb tosses it up and bowls it around off. A wrong 'un which probably is picked up by Asif as he winds up for a big slog sweep over the leg side. But ends up getting an inside edge onto the pads.
Very full and on middle, Asif keeps it out on the leg side and the mid-wicket fielder makes the stop.
Turning down the leg side, Malik plays it with the spin to deep square leg for a single.
A bit on the shorter side outside off, Asif gets back and  plays it in front of square on the off side. The ball goes through the gap and he gets off the mark with a run.
Quicker and fuller on off, it's pushed calmly down through mid on for a run.
Asif Ali is the new batsman. This boy can hit it to all parts. A very strong hitter. Meanwhile, Mujeeb Ur Rahman is back into the attack as well, he has one over left.

OUT! Bowled off a full toss, can you believe it? Naib lures the batsman with a juicy delivery, slower in pace, Sarfraz makes space to hammer it through the line but misses the ball completely. The stumps are shattered and this game once again is thrown wide open. 42 needed off 30 balls.
Follows the batsman down the leg side with a low full toss, Malik brings down a straight bat and forces it down to long on for a run.
Wide! Naib attempts the back of the hand slower ball but ends up serving it too wide outside off. Malik allows it through.
Slower one in line of the stumps, it's tapped down on the off side for one.
Again a low full toss outside off, Malik drives it square of the wicket on the off side for a sharp single.
Wide! Drifting down the leg side, Malik fails to get any bat behind it.

A run out chance... MISSED! Slower short ball around off, it's pulled across the line and to the left side of the mid-wicket fielder inside the ring. He attacks the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end. Naib tries to collect it but misses and breaks the stumps with his hands. The replays show that a direct hit would have consumed Sarfraz.
A low full toss on off, Malik clips it straight towards mid-wicket and scampers across for a quick single.
Gulbadin Naib is back for another burst. 49 needed off 36 balls.
5 from this as it ends with a single. Malik punches it down to long on.
A couple! Excellent cricket, excellent running! Shoaib works this googly towards mid-wicket. He plays it with soft hands and the batsmen run two.
Left alone! Strange, maybe they are looking to play Rashid out. This is outside off, Malik shoulders arms to it.
The googly, slightly shorter in length. Sarfraz goes for the pull but the ball skids through. He mistimes the pull towards square leg for a run.
On the shorter side on middle, Malik punches it down to long on for a run.
A dot to begin! The leggie on off, Malik tries to defend but gets an outside edge towards short third man.
Rashid Khan is back into the attack. He has three overs to go, three crucial overs.
This is bowled on a length, Sarfraz drives it to mid off. A dot to end another good over! 5 from this one also.
On middle, Malik works it towards mid-wicket. He sets off for a run. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses.
A slower bouncer on middle, it bounces like a tennis ball, above the batsman's head. Wide signaled.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total. The umpire though feels there was no bat and has signaled it as a leg bye.
A low full toss on middle, Malik drives it down to long on for a run.
On a length around off, Sarfraz tries to defend but gets an inside edge beside the stumps. Malik calls for a run and they complete it.

A huge appeal but not given! Shortish outside off, Sarfraz tries to guide it through point but gets beaten. The ball moves a long way after passing the bat and hence an appeal. The umpire however, is not fooled.
Aftab Alam is back on.
Sarfraz chops it towards point and takes a run. A good over by Mujeeb, they needed this one, especially after the last one being expensive. Just 5 and a wicket from it.
Quicker on middle, SA blocks it out.
Again short on the stumps, Sarfraz cuts it but finds backward point.
Malik eases it down to long on and takes a run.
Off the mark with a three! Very nicely played. Waited for it and guides it through short third man. Some good running helps the batsmen run three.
Sarfraz Ahmed, the skipper, is the new man in.

OUT! In the air... taken! Afghanistan are still hanging in there. Haris Sohail departs for a low score. A poor shot, to be honest. The last over went for 11 runs and this risk was not needed. He though still takes it, that too without picking the googly and tries to hit the ball over the long on fence. There is no timing on the shot and it goes towards long on, where Ihsanullah takes a decent catch after moving swiftly to his right. Another 64 needed in 53.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. One run added to the total. 11 from the over, a very expensive one.

TWO BYES! Afghanistan just about losing it now! First, Sohail is completely deceived by a slower ball. It goes to Shahzad on the bounce. He parries it towards square leg. The batsmen go for a run, the fielder picks it up and has a needless shy at the non-striker's end. He misses and the batsmen run an overthrow.
Smart! They have already got the runs needed per over and now they need not take any risk. Malik drops it towards point and takes a single.
WIDE! Pressure getting to Naib. He bowls a wide ball outside off. An extra added to the total.
Now a dot! On a length around off, Malik pushes it to covers.
Another classy shot, not for a boundary but for a couple. Full and on off, Malik opens the face of the bat and drives it square on the off side for a brace. 6 from the first two balls.

FOUR! Poor ball and put away! A nothing delivery, short, it had no pace on it. Malik had all the time in the world to pull it through backward square leg and the ball goes into the fence. Ideal start to this over, pressure on the bowler now.
Powerplay 3 is signaled. Now a maximum of 5 fielders are allowed outside the ring till the end of the match. Gulbadin Naib comes back to bowl.
So, two dots to end the over! On the stumps, Sohail blocks it out. 75 needed off the last 10 now.
On the shorter side and on middle, Malik pushes it back to the bowler.
Guides it towards short third man and takes a run.
The batsman has driven that ball straight back. One run added to the total.
Flighted ball on off, Malik drives it to covers for a run.
Flatter and quicker on off, Sohail, off the back foot, punches it through covers for a run.
Mujeeb to have another go.
On a length around off, the batsman defends it. A dot to end the over. 5 from it. 79 more needed off 66 balls.
Nicely waited for the slower ball to come to him and then guided it through short third man for a run.
Slower bouncer! Malik swivels and pulls it all along the ground towards deep square leg for a run.
Fuller in length on middle, Sohail strokes it through mid on for a run.
Shorter in length outside off, Malik punches it through covers for a run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They have run through for a single.
Aftab Alam is back into the attack.
Tosses it up on off, Malik lunges and keeps it out.
The googly on off, Malik defends it off the back foot.

EDGED AND SHORT! Rashid creating a lot of problems. Another leg spinner and at a quicker pace. Shoaib Malik goes back and tries to defend but the ball takes the outside edge and goes on the bounce to first slip.

DROPPED? Not sure! It's bowled quicker and outside off on the shorter side. Malik tries to cut but he seems to have missed. Shahzad behind the stumps fails to collect it. There is some noise but not sure of what... Wait on, the replays show there was an outside edge. So, a chance goes down begging. Need all these to be taken, they do not have a lot to defend. Every half chance has to be taken.
He picks the leggie this time and flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.

EDGY FOUR! Sohail will take it with both hands. It is short and quick outside off, Haris tries to cut but the ball goes off the outside edge, well wide of the fielder at short third man and races away. So, after the wicket, runs are coming thick and fast.
A length ball on off, defended towards point.

Direct hit was the need of the hour! Full and on middle, Malik clips it through mid-wicket and returns for the second run. The fielder from the deep sends across the throw at the striker's end, not an accurate one, as Malik dives in. The keeper collects the ball but fails to throw it onto the stumps.
Pitches it up and outside off, it's driven through covers for a couple of runs.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Buck up, Afghanistan. You have the momentum at the moment, don't let it slip with a sloppy piece of fielding. A late dab down to third man by Malik and it races through. Mujeeb in the deep rushes across to his left, puts in a slide but makes a complete mess after that. It sneaks past him to meet the fence.

Good length delivery outside off, Malik reaches out for it and steers it through point. As soon as he hit it, he knew there were a couple of runs. Calls for it and completes it with ease. That's all experience does for you.
Malik has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Another appeal but the umpire shakes his head. The leg spinner again, Sohail tries to block but the ball kisses the inside edge and goes onto hit Sohail's pads.
The leggie, Sohail tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Another googly outside off, Malik tries to defend but gets an inside edge through square leg for a run. He gets off the mark.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The googly on off, Malik defends it off the back foot.
Shoaib Malik walks out to the middle.

OUT! Azam is short and Afghanistan are back in the game. It is Rashid Khan who gets Pakistan's talisman. But credit has to be given to Shahzad as he was lightning quick behind the stumps. It is the leggie from Rashid and it is just behind a driving length. Azam goes for the drive but the ball turns and beats the outside edge. Azam loses his balance and Shahzad, behind the stumps, whips the bails off in a flash before appealing. He seems to be pretty confident but the umpire takes it upstairs. Replays roll in and they show that Azam is out of his crease. Azam departs after playing a very good innings and now both the set batsmen are back in the hut. 100 more needed now.
Big moment in the game! Shahzad with some neat work with the gloves may just have got Azam stumped. They have gone upstairs to check. Let's see.
Gets off strike now by easing it down to long on for a run but he was not at his best today. He finishes with figures of 10-0-50-0.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Three dot balls as Nabi once again bowls it on the pads, Sohail flicks it to short fine leg.
Angles this into the pads, Sohail works it to mid-wicket.
Flatter on off, Sohail pushes it to covers.
A googly has been pushed right back past the bowler for a single. End of a successful over for Afghanistan, 3 runs and a wicket from it.
Appeal for an lbw, not entertained. A leg spinner landing around off and turning back in, Sohail tries to defend but gets an INSIDE EDGE onto the pads.
Fuller and on middle, knocked down to long on for a single.
Haris Sohail is the new batsman.

OUT! Imam is well short of the crease. Is this the turning point of the match? Afghanistan are delighted. They still believe. 100 odd runs to play with. Coming to the delivery, it's full and around off, Imam pushes it gently to cover-point and rushes across for a single. Najibullah Zadran attacks the ball inside the circle and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end. They appeal, Rashid is all smiles and the umpire goes upstairs. The replays roll in and tell us why the leggie was smiling. The century partnership has been broken. Brilliance in the field has provided them with a breakthrough. Can the bowlers step up now and deliver the goods?
Direct hit at the bowler's end. Afghanistan are ecstatic. They think they have got the breakthrough. It's referred upstairs. Is Imam short of the crease?
Too full and on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for one.
Floated full ball on off, driven through covers for a single.
Rashid Khan comes back for another shot.

Do we have an interesting chase on our hands or what! Pakistan, with only a wicket down, look the favorites currently. However, this is cricket, and it's not over until the last ball is bowled or the last run is scored. A wicket or two, a few tight overs and the match will again be in the balance. Afghanistan desperately need quick wickets and restrict the flow of runs to build pressure on the Pakistan batsmen. Let's see what happens after the break...
Time for the 2nd and final Drinks break.
FOUR! Into the 80s goes Imam! He goes down on one knee and with the angle sweeps it over mid-wicket and to the fence. He got into position very early, maybe he per-meditated that shot.
On off, it has been defended.
Flighted ball on off, Imam strokes it towards covers.

Fires it in on the pads, Azam flicks it through square leg and takes a run. This is too easy, Afghanistan need to do something different. Maybe ask the spinners to flight the ball a little. Also attack a bit more.
On the pads, the batsman works it through mid-wicket and takes a run.
Uses his feet but Nabi sees that. He bowls it short. Imam waits for it and works it towards mid-wicket.
On the stumps, Azam lunges and defends it.
Eases this through mid on and takes a run.
The batsman has played it fine down the leg side.
Imam uses Mujeeb's pace and guides it through short third man. The batsmen run two.
Attacks the stumps, the batsman keeps it out.
Flatter and quicker outside off, Imam cuts it to point.
Mujeeb is back.
Azam works it with the turn towards square leg for a single.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Opens the face of his bat at the very last moment and guides it through point for a run.
Floats it up on off, Azam drives it to covers.
Lovely! Just pushes it back past the bowler and takes a run. Really clever, they are milking the bowlers.
Azam flicks it through square leg and takes a quick run. Singles are all they need now.
Mohammad Nabi is back into the attack.
Tucks the next ball through backward square leg and takes a run. 10 from the over and Pakistan need another 118 from 120 balls.
FOUR! Azam now has decided to step on the accelerator. He stands tall, waits for the slower ball and pulls it over the mid-wicket fielder and into the fence.
A slower ball yorker on middle, Imam digs it out towards mid-wicket for a quick run.
How is that for timing? Wow! That was right off the middle, through covers for a brace.
A low full toss on off, Azam mistimes it towards wide mid off for a run. It was the slower one and hence, Azam could not time it.
Smart batting! They know they don't have to do anything expansive so Imam just guides it down to third man and jogs to the other end.
Gulbadin Naib is back on.
Gets away with a poor delivery. Short and on off, pulled across the line but straight to the fielder inside the ring at mid-wicket.
Shortish and on off, punched through extra cover for a run.
Wide! Flatter and quicker, skidding down the leg side, the batsman fails to flick and it goes off Shahzad's pads towards short fine leg. They cross.
Too full and on middle, it's eased down to long on for one.
Fires it in on middle, fuller in length, it's hit back to the bowler.
Full and on the pads, clipped through square leg for a couple of runs. Excellent running between the wickets.
Flighted delivery, landing very full on off, Imam pushes it back to the bowler.
Mujeeb Ur Rahman is back on with Afghanistan in desperate need of a wicket.

FOUR! Ends the over in style! An excellent one for Pakistan. It is short and outside off, Azam rocks back and slaps it through the cover region. The ball races away. 12 runs from the over and Pakistan are well on course now.
And now does the right thing by working it through the leg side and getting to the other end.

SIX! Going, going and gone! That should release a lot of pressure. Top shot! He uses his feet, gets to the pitch of the delivery and lofts it over mid on. The fielder is in the ring. However, even if he had been on the rope, it would not have made a difference as it has gone all the way.

Fifty for Azam now, 8th in ODIs. Another good innings by the talented Pakistan player. He gets there by clipping it through mid-wicket for a run. These two are doing it nicely and have not given any opening to the Afghan bowlers.
With the turn, Azam works it to square leg.
On the shorter side, Azam works it to mid-wicket.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.

NOT OUT! Azam is well in! He drives it back towards Rashid. Khan does really well to make a diving stop and then scores a direct hit at the striker's end. The players appeal and the umpire takes it upstairs. Replay shows, Azam is in.
A direct hit and the umpire takes it upstairs. Azam is the man in question. He seems to be relaxed.
Slightly short again, Imam cuts it through covers for a run. Not been at his best until now, he is bowling too short.
Slightly short and Azam rocks onto the back foot quickly and pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
Very full on middle, Imam jams it out towards long on for a run.
On the stumps, worked to mid-wicket.

Slight stoppage in play! Babar Azam is down and receiving some stretching from the Pakistani physio. Maybe, cramps. The players are doing well to keep themselves hydrated whenever the opportunity comes. The game situation currently - 150 needed off 144 balls.

Drags his length short and bowls it wide outside off, Babar cuts it behind point and scampers back for the second run. A better throw from the deep could have made it interesting. Afghanistan losing intensity in the field. Usually they are very energetic and accurate.
Jumps out of the crease to a full ball on middle and pushes it back to the bowler.
On middle, worked on the leg side but he found the mid-wicket fielder.

Chance of a run out! Missed. Quicker and flatter on off, Imam gets forward and softly plays it towards covers for a brisk run. The fielder misses his shy at the striker's end otherwise it could have been tight. Also, Shahzad after collecting the throw failed to take the bails off. Sloppy.
Continues from 'round the wicket for the right-hander as well. He serves it full and on middle, it's eased through mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted full ball on off, it's turned to the right of short fine leg for a quick single.
Mohammad Nabi is back into the attack.
The skidder outside off, Azam tries to cut but is beaten.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Another short ball outside off, Imam cuts it towards point and gets to the other end.

Fifty for Imam, second for him in ODIs to go with 4 hundreds. This has really been an excellent innings from the youngster. He has to grind it out there and is now reaping the rewards. He plays this with soft hands towards backward square leg and takes a brace.
Flatter on off, the batsman somehow keeps it out as the ball stays a touch low.
Very full on off, Azam drives it to covers.
On middle, worked to mid-wicket.

The 100 for Pakistan and the 100-run stand is up between the pair as well. Not a convincing way to reach there. Imam comes down the track and swings but the ball takes the outside edge and goes to third man for a run.
The leg cutter outside off, Imam cuts it past the diving fielder at point for another brace.
Fuller in length on middle, the batsman drives it back to the bowler.
Well fielded! The slower ball, Azam cuts it hard towards covers. The fielder there dives and makes a very good stop. Saves a few runs for his team. The batsmen in the meantime take one.
On a length around off, Azam drives it to covers.
Azam easily pushes it down to long on for a run. Another 162 needed in 162 balls.
Almost! The leg spinner, pitches on middle and then gets it to skid through. Imam at the very end, gets his bat down and works it through square leg for a run.
The leg spinner outside off, Imam guides it to point.
Another wide signalled! This time outside off, another attempted googly.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Quicker and flatter outside off, Imam guides it towards point where the fielder makes a very good stop.
On the shorter side, it is pushed down to long on for a run.
WIDE! Down the leg side, Shahzad fails to collect and the umpire stretches his arms.
Shortish and outside off, cut from the back foot to deep point for one. Pakistan are going at ease currently. 167 needed off 168 balls.
Slower one, on a length outside off, quietly played down to third man for a single. A direct hit scored from the deep but nothing doing. However, Shahzad let out a stifled appeal.
Straighter in line, worked off the pads to the leg side, not in the gap.
Shortish on middle and leg, Azam tries working it off his hips but fails to middle it. It drops near the surface and they steal a run.
FOUR! Risky but effective. Naib offers width outside off, Babar sits deep inside the crease and plays at it very late. Does quite well to beat the diving keeper and find the boundary.
Slower short ball outside off, crunched off the back foot to sweeper cover and he ran the first run hard. They put pressure on the fielder in the deep who fumbled and allowed the second run.
Gulbadin Naib comes back into the attack.
On the stumps, kept out. So just two from Khan's first over. Exactly what is expected off him. Afghanistan would hope he can contain the runs as well as pick wickets.

BEATEN! Not a good shot to play against Rashid. He is too quick and his lengths are also quite deceptive. Flatter and quicker outside off, Imam goes for the cut but is late into the shot and hence gets beaten.
Azam now goes back and flicks it through square leg for a single.
Imam goes back and tucks it through square leg for a run.

Quicker and shorter again, Imam tries to pull but is a little late on the shot. He mistimes it to mid-wicket. Azam wants a run but is sent back. The mid-wicket fielder has a shy but misses by a long way.
Quicker and shorter outside off, Imam cuts it to point.
The time has arrived! Rashid Khan is into the attack. This is where the real game begins. How Pakistan tackle Rashid Khan will probably decide the fate of this game!
Another short ball is worked towards fine leg for another single.
Pulls it through in front of square, Rashid is the man in the deep. He is quick but not quick enough to stop the brace.
This time, he lets the ball come to him and tucks it around the corner for a run.

LEADING EDGE BUT SAFE! That was close. Heart in mouth moment for Azam. He once again closes the face of his bat a touch early. Gets a leading edge which flies past the out stretched hand of the bowler and towards mid off.
Uses his feet but does not get to the pitch of the ball. He pushes it through covers for a run.
Good length around off, this one skids through. Azam plays it late down to third man for a single.

Floated ball on off, Imam skips down the track and drives it back to the bowler. Nabi collects the ball and has an immediate shy at the striker's end. Misses the stumps but anyway, Imam would have been in.
Short and wide outside off, Azam rocks back and slaps it to deep point for one.

Risky single. That's what dot balls do to you. Flighted and full on off, Imam pushes it with gentle hands to cover-point and pinches a single. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses the target.
Quicker and shorter on middle, Imam reads the length a bit late and hits it towards mid-wicket again. Three dot balls.
Full and skidding in from around off, it's flicked on the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.
Flatter and fuller on off, a punchy drive by Imam but the short cover fielder does well to stop it with a dive.
Serves it on a length just outside off, straightening a bit after landing, Babar strokes it through the line but finds the cover fielder. Dot ball to end the over.
Once again a slower delivery by Alam. It's short and on off, Imam pulls it quite nicely to deep mid-wicket. They take a run.
Slower one, short and outside off, it's steered behind point for a single.
On a good length around off, Imam plays it late and dabs it down to third man for another single in this over.
Once again the length is a touch on the shorter side around off, Babar remains back footed and pulls it in front of square leg for one.
A little short in length and around off, Imam crouches a bit and cuts it square of the wicket on the off side. The third man fielder cuts it off and they take a single.
Aftab Alam returns in the attack. They are holding back Rashid Khan at the moment. 191 needed off 198 balls.
Works it with the angle, through the leg side and takes a run.

Time for Drinks. Seems like this match is going to go all the way to the wire. It is still anybody's game though.Pakistan want one big partnership to ride their chase on. Afghanistan, on the other hand, will be eager to break this partnership and penetrate deeper into the Pakistani batting line-up.
WIDE! Down the leg side and it has been wided.
Smart bowling! Seeing the batsman give him the charge, Nabi slows it up. Babar tries to drive but misses. The ball hits his pads and goes towards short fine leg and the batsmen run a leg bye.
Tries to flick but closes the face of the bat a touch early. It takes a soft leading edge to the bowler.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
A little too short outside off, Azam cuts it through point for a couple.
Good running! On the stumps, Imam plays it towards mid on and straightaway goes for a run and completes it.
Imam plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. One run added to the total.
Oohhh...this one stays seriously low after landing on a length around off. It's angled in and Imam does well to crouch and block it. Always kept his eyes on the ball and that was the key there.
Feeds the batsman with a short and wide ball outside off, Azam cracks it through cover-point and Rashid Khan is lightning quick in the field. Only a run taken.
Gets on the front foot to play the cover drive but the fielder inside the ring does superbly to stop the ball with a dive.
Shortish and on off, Babar goes hard at it this time and mistimes his shot towards covers. He's a touch-batsman, should concentrate on timing rather than power.
Delicate. A length delivery around off, Babar delays his shot and at the last moment runs it down fine to third man for a brace.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.

SIX! This should get him going! Lovely hit. Straight as an arrow! Dances down the track, does not get to the pitch of it but still lofts it over the bowler's head. The timing is such that it carries over the ropes.

Imam eases it through the mid on region, exactly from where the fielder was pushed back, for a run. 50-run stand comes up and it is a vital one as Pakistan lost a wicket really early. They would want the two to continue.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A little short outside off, Imam tries to cut but ends up mistiming it to covers.
Uses his feet but does not get to the pitch of it. He drives it to covers.
Pulled nicely, all along the ground to the man at deep square leg for a run.
Babar tries to break the shackles here. The slower ball on middle, Azam goes for the hoick but gets it off the inner half towards deep square leg for a run.
The ultra slow delivery says Ramiz Raja on air. It was short and outside off, Imam waits for it and then cuts it hard but finds sweeper cover, so only a run.
Once again, he plays it late. Babar with an angled bat, guides it down to third man for a run.
Walks across and flicks it through square leg for a run.
Very full on middle, Imam drives it back towards the bowler who makes a half-stop but no runs conceded.
Good running! Imam taps this towards covers and the batsmen scamper through for a run. Rotation of strike is very important as the boundaries are not coming at will.
Again very full on middle, Azam eases it down to long on for a run.
A little too full this time, Imam drives it nicely to the man at long off for a run.
Quicker this time on middle, Imam keeps it out.
A little wide outside off and also slower through the air. Imam drives it square on the off side.
Gives it air on off, Imam defends it onto the ground.
A dot to end another tight over! Azam punches this to covers. He needs to rotate strike here. Getting into a shell currently, on 12 from 37 balls.
Well bowled! A well-disguised slower ball outside off, Azam is early into the cut shot and gets beaten.
Driven on the up but once again finds the fielder. Babar should not get frustrated as he is not finding the gaps.
On the shorter side, Azam chops it towards point. He wanted a run but Imam once again refuses.

OVERTHROW! Not sure this was needed. It was shaping up to be a dot ball as it was driven back to the bowler who had a needless shy. The throw was a wild one, Shahzad only managed to parry it towards fine leg and the batsmen run an overthrow.
Slower ball on the pads, Azam flicks it through backward square leg for a run.
With the turn but against the angle, Azam flicks it through mid-wicket for a run. So a tight start by Nabi, kept attacking the stumps and gave nothing away. He will continue to do so.
From around the wicket now, he bowls it on middle, Azam pushes it back to the bowler.
Imam strokes it down to long on for a run.
This is eased down to long on for a run.
Swept but straight to the short fine leg fielder. A little to his left or right and it would have been a boundary. Azam is struggling to find the gaps here.
Slower through the air on middle, Azam strokes it back to the bowler.

Powerplay 2 has been signaled. A maximum of four fielders will now be allowed outside the ring till the end of the 40th over. The experienced and wily offie, Mohammad Nabi, comes into the attack now. We are in for an interesting passage of play.

From around the wicket, he angles it into the batsman. Imam blocks it onto the ground. End of Powerplay 1 and both the teams will be content with the start. Afghanistan have not conceded a lot of runs and Pakistan have not lost a lot of wickets.
Delicate but risky also! This one comes back in very late. Azam plays it at the last moment towards third man for a run.
Crisply driven but once again cannot find the gap. 4 dots in this over so far.
Good length again on off, Babar guides it towards point. He wanted a run but is sent back. The point fielder has a shy at the keeper's end but misses.
Slightly short around off, Babar cuts it to point. This was a little too close to play that shot.
Starts off with a very full ball on off, no swing on offer. Babar Azam drives it towards covers.
Gulbadin Naib is into the attack.
Full and on middle, knocked down the ground but straight to mid on.
A googly around off, Imam lunges and defends. He is reading Mujeeb well.
Spinning back in a bit from around off, it's on the shorter side and Imam keeps it out towards mid-wicket.
A touch flatter and fuller on off, it's driven off the front foot to mid off where the fielder fumbles and makes the single easy.
Turning down the leg side, Imam reads it well and works it with the spin to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted and full around off, Imam defends it off his front foot.
Goes back to bowling length around the off stump line. Azam defends it.
FOUR! CRACKED! Very, very easy on the eye that one! A little short on middle, Azam stands tall and pulls it through mid-wicket and you need not run for those.
Well bowled! On a length and this one comes back in. Azam defends it onto the ground.
On off, Azam wants to drop and run but is sent back by his partner.
Shortish and outside off, Imam guides it down to third man for a run.
On a length around off, Imam defends it to point.
The skipper, Afghan is off the ground. He went off yesterday also, maybe the heat is getting to him.
Tosses it up on off, Azam lunges and blocks it out.
Imam is deep in the crease, waits for the ball and works it towards square leg. The fielder there makes a good diving stop but can't stop the single.
Gives it air on off, Imam drives it towards wide long on for a couple. He is looking good out there.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Down the leg side, Imam goes for the sweep but misses. Shahzad tries to put the umpire off with an appeal but the umpire is spot on by signaling it as a WIDE.
Flatter on off, the batsman pushes it to covers.
The slider on the pads, Imam finds mid-wicket with the flick.
A dot to end it but he would feel he got away! It was there to be hit, a little short and a lot of width on offer outside off. Azam slaps it but finds the fielder at cover-point. A maiden.
Lovely stuff, on a length around middle, Babar is solid in defense. This has been a very good over by Alam till now. One more ball to go, needs to end it well.
Another classic punch but straight to the fielder at cover-point.
Not sure if this one stayed a touch low or Azam played back to a ball he should have come forward. On a length around off, Azam at the last moment, gets his bat down in time in defense.
Good shot but no runs! On the shorter side, Azam hits it into the ground and the ball bounces in front of the point fielder. He collects it over his head.
Back of a length on off, Azam punches it to the man at covers.
Imam might have picked this leg spinner as he rocks back and works it to mid-wicket. So the misfield spoils the over, or else it was another tight one by Mujeeb.
Again, this one was flatter and quicker, Imam blocks it out.
Darts it on off, Imam goes back and defends it.
Down the leg side, Imam fails to flick and the umpire calls it a wide. Good take by Shahzad.

MISFIELD AND FOUR AGAIN! This is just not done! You need to back your bowlers, especially someone who is bowling so well. It is short and outside off, Imam cuts it towards point. Alam there lets it through his hands and the ball races away.
Quicker this time but it is a touch shorter in length. Azam goes back and punches it down to long on for a run.
Slower through the air, pitches it around off. Azam lunges and defends it.
A quick single and they make it! 6 from the over! Fuller in length and on middle, Babar strokes it towards mid on for a quick run.
A little too straight on the pads, Imam flicks it through square leg for a single.
Very good! Like that! On a length around off, Imam defends it onto the ground.
A little too wide outside off, left alone. Alam needs to keep it tight and provide good support to Mujeeb.

MISFIELD AND FOUR! Aftab is leaking runs here. He bowls it short and outside off, Imam cuts but gets an outside edge towards third man. The fielder there runs to his right, dives but fails to stop the ball.
Good length by the bowler and the line is also fine. On off, kept out.
6 dots which means it is a maiden. Another loopy ball outside off, Babar goes for the drive but gets an inside edge to short fine leg.
This was right off the middle but to the man at covers. 5 dots in a row.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Tosses it up again, Azam strokes it to mid off again.
Flatter and on the shorter side, Azam punches it to mid off.

NOT OUT! The impact is outside the line! Afghanistan lose their only review very early. Credit to the umpire though as that is an excellent decision. Mujeeb bowls an inswinging yorker, yes you read it right, an inswinging yorker. It comes back in late with plenty of drift. Azam gets his front foot forward and across as he tries to defend. But he misses to get hit on the right boot. Mujeeb appeals but the umpire shakes his head. The bowler wants it to be reviewed. All the Afghanistan players want it to be referred and Afghan does so. He signals the 'T'. Time for the replays and it shows the impact to be outside off.
Howzzat? The umpire shakes his head. Mujeeb straightaway wants it to be reviewed. Azam is the man in question. Huge moment in the game. Impact can be an issue.
Lands it on a length on middle, Imam plays it down safely towards mid-wicket. A good over for Pakistan, 12 runs coming off it.
Wide! Turning out to be a really long over. Down the leg side, once again Imam fails to make any use of it.

FOUR! Stylish! Imam is in really good form and this shot proves it. Alam drops it short outside off, angling away, Imam picks the length in a trice and hammer-pulls it past the diving mid-wicket fielder for a boundary.
Wide! Wrong line by Alam and he will have to reload. Slips in a length ball down the leg side, Imam tries to get some wood behind it but fails. Shahzad fumbles but no extra run conceded.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Imam gets behind the line and watchfully defends it.

Edged but safe! Shortish in length and around off, Azam stays back to play inside the line but is squared up. Gets an outside edge in the process and it runs wide of first slip to third man. A single taken.
The length is on the shorter side again, outside off, Imam plays it late and steers it down behind backward point for a run.
FOUR! Great start from Imam! He receives a short delivery first up around off, stays on the back foot and pulls it with authority to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Babar Azam walks in to bat. Also Aftab Alam will bowl from the other end with the second new ball.

OUT! Mujeeb strikes in the first over itself. The dangerous Zaman goes for another duck. Dream start for Afghanistan. This is very full around the off pole. Zaman picks the wrong ball to play the sweep shot. He misses and the ball hits his pads. The players appeal and the umpire, after giving it a thought, raises the finger. Fakhar walks up to his partner and has a chat but then does not take the review. Wonder why! Because the impact could have been an issue there. In fact, the Hawk Eye, later on, shows that the impact was outside off. Zaman will be kicking himself after looking at the replays. Afghanistan though will rejoice as they are off to a great start.
Again, shuffles across the stumps and blocks it out.
Zaman with a new tactic, shuffles across the line and defends the ball on the stumps.
BEATEN! That was a peach! Zaman had no clue about which way the ball was going. Mujeeb floats it up around off, it pitches and straightens. Zaman plays inside the line and gets beaten.
Slightly short and outside off, Zaman cuts it to point.
Right on the money first up. Slower through the air on middle, Zaman works it towards square leg.

We are back for the chase and trust me it is going to be an exciting one. The two Pakistan openers, Fakhar Zaman and Imam-ul-Haq make their way out to the middle. The former will be on strike and he will face Mujeeb Ur Rahman who will bowl with the first new ball. Here we go...
